definitions: François-Marie Arouet (1694–1778), known by his nom de plume Voltaire, was a French Enlightenment writer, historian, and philosopher famous for his wit, his attacks on the established Catholic Church, and his advocacy of freedom of speech, freedom of religion, and separation of church and state.
examples: Voltaire's writings influenced both the American and French Revolutions.
Many consider Voltaire a foundational figure of the Enlightenment.
